Implications by form: weak -> technical analysis fails, fundamental and private information may still give an edge; semi-strong -> fundamental analysis of public data also fails, only private information may give an edge; strong -> no information gives an edge. Clients who think markets are easy to beat overtrade and chase recent winners, adding costs and (in taxable accounts) realized gains

Limits of the EMH: anomalies (size, value, momentum) may be risk premiums or disappear after publication; behavioural finance shows over- and underreaction; large heavily followed markets close to semi-strong efficient, less-followed segments may leave room for active managers
